feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that $y$ is a composite function:

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{h},\,h=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}h}=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{h},\,\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}x}=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}h}\cdot \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{h}\cdot (-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =-2{e}^{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{e}^{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$
